messages:
incident-bot: @jordan HIGH-SEV page — AegisPay (dedicated: ded-aegis-us-east) is seeing model errors & timeouts (~40% 5xx) for v1.3.2 across their VPC endpoint. Auto-fallback to safe variants triggered but client reports degraded outputs. Link: https://internal.incidents/1768001234 :rotating_light:

jordan: acked. grabbing context, paging SRE. sam are you up?

sam: on my way, pinged the oncall runbook. quick summary pls — who changed what?

maya: saw elevated tail latency on the dedicated pool at 15:02 UTC, plus repeated KV cache misses after a redeploy minutes earlier. Customer said they pinned to v1.3.2 yesterday, but routing might be serving a quantized fallback `gpt-medium-q4k` intermittently.

jordan: @vlad can you confirm whether AegisPay is pinned on the control plane or if our smart-routing has overridden to safevariant? Customer console shows pin v1.3.2, but runtime logs show `select_variant: gpt-medium-q4k` for some requests.

vlad: Verified: control plane pin present (`tenant_pin: v1.3.2`). However the runtime applied fallback due to OOMs on some GPUs; it swapped to `gpt-medium-q4k` automatically per fallback policy. We have a partial degradation where fallback preserves correctness but customer claims some scoring fields missing.

sam: interesting — so two behaviours: pinned at control plane, but runtime fallback can still swap to compatible safe variant under resource pressure. That matches policy: pin prevents rollouts but not emergency runtime fallback on memory pressure. We need to decide if we override runtime fallback for this tenant to force strict pin (risk of timeouts) or continue safevariant and accept minor output drift.

jordan: @maya and @lucas collect customer impact: what features are broken? Maya?

maya: AegisPay reports fraud-score field missing ~30% of responses, exact JSON path `response.data.fraud_score` null. They rely on that for real-time decisioning — high impact. They prefer correctness over latency.

lucas: from runtime traces: when fallback `gpt-medium-q4k` is used we strip some auxiliary embeddings to save memory which drops `fraud_score` calc. If we force strict pin to v1.3.2 on ded-aegis-us-east we'll likely increase latency and some requests may 504 if OOM persists.

sam: mitigation options (short list):
- A) Force strict pin on the tenant (runtime_config: allow_fallback=false). Pros: preserves v1.3.2 outputs -> fraud_score present. Cons: higher tail latency/possible 5xx.
- B) Keep fallback but patch a lightweight shim to re-run missing fraud calc using cached embeddings (best-effort). Pros: lower risk of 5xx. Cons: engineering work + potential correctness risk.
- C) Move some of AegisPay's traffic to a warm standby pool (dedicated-aegis-standby) with larger memory profile, no fallback. Pros: preserves outputs with headroom. Cons: requires capacity & routing change, takes ~10-15min to shift traffic.

jordan: AegisPay wants correctness. They asked to avoid any variant that strips fraud_score. They accept some latency up to 2x. Recommendation: pursue (A) immediate strict pin + (C) concurrently migrate a small portion (10%) to standby for critical requests & ramp.

vlad: I can flip the runtime flag now for ded-aegis-us-east: `tenant: aegispay, runtime_override: { allow_fallback: false }` — will do but will also track OOM/retries. Executing in 30s.

incident-bot: action taken by vlad at 1768001300 — `allow_fallback=false` applied to tenant aegispay on ded-aegis-us-east. Link to change: https://internal.changes/1768001300

sam: monitoring: tail latency climbed immediately from 120ms to 380ms p95, 504 rate dropped from 40%->18% but backpressure intermittently causes spikes. Memory pressure still visible on GPU-3.

maya: informed AegisPay PD contact (alice@aegispay) about temporary pin + possible latency. They asked for canary traffic to standby pool — sending request to sales/ops for standby allocation.

jordan: sam, run the standby migration plan if standby capacity confirmed. Steps: 1) confirm standby pool provisioned (dedicated-aegis-standby) 2) create route rule: if header `x-critical=true` -> standby pool 3) shift 10% by weight ctrl-plane 4) monitor fraud_score presence and latency 5) escalate if 504 > 5%

lucas: prepping a quick shim (B-lite) that will attempt to reconstruct fraud_score from last good KV entry if missing — low risk fallback while standby ramps. ETA ~25min.

sam: updating incident doc with timeline and action items. Also tagging infra to watch GPU eviction logs.

vlad: note: we should also consider adding a tenant-level SLO override: increase CPU/GPU soft-limits for pinned tenants to reduce auto-fallback triggers. Filing a follow-up RFC.

jordan: handoff: i'm oncall until 1830 UTC, after that sam takes over. Current state: strict pin applied, standby requested, shim in progress. Customer notified. Next update in 15m or on any regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: update: last_message_ts set to 1768001530 — thread active.
